OnPlay.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-28. The attack is faithful and the block prop set is right (`ValueProp.Move`, powered, so not in G1's blast radius). THE BLOCK AMOUNT IS COMPUTED FROM A DIFFERENT QUANTITY, but only by ONE of the two terms the original entry named. C# gains `attackCommand.Results.SelectMany(r => r).Sum(r => r.TotalDamage + r.OverkillDamage)` (Fisticuffs.cs:32) with `TotalDamage => BlockedDamage + UnblockedDamage` (DamageResult.cs:63), `UnblockedDamage = currentHp - CurrentHp` and `OverkillDamage = num - currentHp` on a kill (Creature.LoseHpInternal, Creature.cs:445-457) — i.e. blocked + hp-actually-lost + overkill = the ENTIRE post-modifier damage the attack put out. The sim uses the return value of `DamageCmd.deal` (colorless_attacks.py:103-110), which is `hp_lost` (cmds.py:196). NOT A DIVERGENCE (do not re-open): the OVERKILL half. `hp_lost` is the post-block, post-`modify_hp_lost` amount and is NEVER clamped to the target's HP — cmds.py:153 seeds it from `amount`, cmds.py:166 runs `modify_hp_lost`, and cmds.py:172 clamps only `target.hp = max(0, target.hp - hp_lost)`, leaving `hp_lost` itself intact — so the sim already equals C#'s UnblockedDamage + OverkillDamage. EXECUTED: hitting a 5-HP enemy with Fisticuffs (7 damage) grants 7 block in the sim, exactly matching C#'s 5 + 2. STILL OPEN, and this is what the gap now is: BLOCKED DAMAGE IS DROPPED. cmds.py:154-157 subtracts `absorbed = min(target.block, amount)` from `hp_lost` before returning it, so C#'s `BlockedDamage` term never reaches the block gain. Observable and ordinary: hit an enemy holding 20 block for 7 and the game grants 7 block while the sim grants 0 — EXECUTED, and the sim's own `test/test_colorless.py:104-108` (`test_fisticuffs_gains_no_block_when_fully_blocked`) asserts the divergent 0, so that legacy test must be updated with the fix. LIVE — Fisticuffs is a ported Uncommon colorless Attack and enemy block is routine. The fix shape: `DamageCmd.deal` must surface the blocked component (or a DamageResult-shaped return) so the card can sum blocked + hp_lost. RATIONALE CITES THIRD FILES (rule 7): DamageResult.cs, Creature.cs and cmds.py are not hashed by this record. The issue it replaced read: The attack is faithful and the block prop set is right (`ValueProp.Move`, powered, so not in G1's blast radius). THE BLOCK AMOUNT IS COMPUTED FROM A DIFFERENT QUANTITY. C# gains `attackCommand.Results.SelectMany(r => r).Sum(r => r.TotalDamage + r.OverkillDamage)` (Fisticuffs.cs:32), and those two fields are precisely defined: `TotalDamage => BlockedDamage + UnblockedDamage` (DamageResult.cs:64) with `UnblockedDamage = currentHp - CurrentHp` and `OverkillDamage = num - currentHp` when the blow kills (Creature.LoseHpInternal, Creature.cs:445-457). So C#'s figure is blocked + hp-actually-lost + overkill, i.e. the ENTIRE post-modifier damage the attack put out. The sim uses the return value of `DamageCmd.deal`, which is `hp_lost` (cmds.py:126) -- the middle term only. It therefore grants LESS block than the game whenever the target had block or was overkilled. Observable and ordinary: hit a 5-HP enemy for 7 and the game grants 7 block while the sim grants 5; hit an enemy holding 10 block for 7 and the game grants 7 while the sim grants 0. LIVE -- Fisticuffs is a ported Uncommon colorless Attack, enemy block is routine, and overkill is the normal case late in a fight.
